skill.name: managing-branches
skill.description: Plan, validate, and automate Git branch workflows, including Gitflow, GitHub Flow, release branches, hotfixes, and worktrees.
skill.summary: Manage Git branch strategy, naming rules, flow validation, releases, hotfixes, and worktrees.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: No malware, exfiltration, or prompt injection attempt was found. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, Git examples, configuration dictionaries, and transparent Git helper scripts. Residual risk is operational: some helper commands can push, tag, delete branches, or create worktrees in custom paths.

remediation.issue: Branch completion can push, tag, and delete branches without final confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run mode and require explicit confirmation before pushing targets, creating tags, or deleting local and remote branches.

remediation.issue: Custom worktree paths are not restricted to an approved project area.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve custom paths and require they stay under the configured worktree base directory, or require explicit approval for absolute and parent-directory paths.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts expose high-impact Git mutations.
remediation.suggestion: Document side effects near each command and encourage users to review planned Git operations before execution.

content.value_statement: Complex Git workflows create inconsistent branches and risky merges. This skill guides branch strategy, naming, validation, and worktree operations across Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains and compares Gitflow, GitHub Flow, GitLab Flow, trunk-based, and simple workflows.
Generates branch names from branch type, issue number, and description.
Validates branch names, allowed merge targets, and flow compliance.
Creates, lists, removes, and cleans Git worktrees through helper scripts.
Initializes branching configuration templates for common team workflows.
Guides release, hotfix, feature, and cleanup procedures.
limitations: It cannot bypass repository permissions, branch protection, or failed status checks.
It depends on an existing Git repository and locally available Git commands.
Remote pushes, branch deletion, and worktree removal require careful user approval.
It does not deploy code or replace CI/CD release systems.

The skill identifies release branch targets, tag timing, cleanup rules, and checks needed before merging to production.

best_practices: Review the planned Git commands before allowing the agent to run helper scripts.
Keep branch strategy configuration in the repository and review it with the team.
Use dry runs or manual checks before deleting branches or worktrees.
anti_patterns: Do not run finish or cleanup commands with unclear branch names.
Do not place worktrees in sensitive directories or outside approved project paths.
Do not mix Gitflow, trunk-based, and environment branch rules in one repository.

faq.question: Can it create branches automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide or run helper scripts when the user approves. Scripts can change the local Git repository.

faq.question: Which workflows does it support?
faq.answer: It covers Gitflow, GitHub Flow, GitLab Flow, trunk-based development, and simple branch flows.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub?
faq.answer: No. Git commands work locally. GitHub-specific guidance appears only for pull requests, issues, and branch protection.

faq.question: Can it manage worktrees?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains, creates, lists, removes, and cleans worktrees through Git commands and helper scripts.

faq.question: Is it safe for protected branches?
faq.answer: It checks configured policies, but repository permissions and branch protection remain the source of truth.

faq.question: Does it replace release tooling?
faq.answer: No. It coordinates branch flow and tags, but build, deployment, and changelog tools remain separate.
